lina: Heads-up — customer (acct: acme-marketing) says their invoice shows ~3.1k tokens more than the usage dashboard for a streaming chat session earlier today. They used our JS SSE client and cancelled mid-response.

lina: Quick repro notes they sent: one long streaming completion, client hits cancel after ~6s, then reconnects, then final partial event appears in our billing logs twice. They attached request_id `r_2026-03-16_92bx` and invoice `INV-ACME-221`. :thinking:

tom: Can you drop the request_id + timeline? We need the ledger entries and the matching dashboard samples. Also cc @amir for runtime counts.

lina: Request: `r_2026-03-16_92bx` (start 2387650000). Their frontend trace:
```
// client trace (simplified)
connect -> GET /v1/generate/stream?model=gpt-open
recv chunk (partial tokens 0..345)
user triggers cancel
client -> abort()
client reconnect -> same session id
recv final chunk (tokens 346..400)
```
They say our dashboard shows 401 tokens total but invoice ledger has 471.

amir: Two quick hypotheses: 1) SSE reconnect path re-emits a trailing delimiter/event that our metering counts as an extra token group; 2) our finalization hook (when connection closes) runs twice on abort+reconnect and double-counts the last output. I'll pull server traces.

jess: Adding logs from the serving runtime around that request id — note the `emit_trailer` call at 2387650035 and again at 2387650040 on the same request handle:
```
[2387650035] request=r_2026-03-16_92bx tokens_emitted=345 state=streaming emit_trailer=true
[2387650040] request=r_2026-03-16_92bx tokens_emitted=400 state=closing emit_trailer=true
[2387650040] billing: record_stream_tokens(request=r_2026-03-16_92bx, tokens=400)
[2387650041] billing: record_stream_tokens(request=r_2026-03-16_92bx, tokens=71)
```
jess: That last line looks wrong — a separate 71 was recorded after the 400 main record. 71 matches the delta we see on the invoice. :alarm_clock:

tom: Is 71 from an internal retry / reconnect path? Could be a re-emit of buffered suffix (we keep a small suffix for safety). If the suffix is re-counted on reconnection and also counted on close, ledger will show 400+71.

lina: Customer says when they cancelled, the client still received one small trailing SSE event labeled `trailer: eof` after reconnect. Their dev posted the exact SSE frames (sanitized):
```
event: message
data: {"chunk":"..."}

event: trailer
data: {"tokens":71, "reason":"truncated"}
```
lina: They claim the dashboard aggregates only the streaming frames while the ledger picks up both the main emission and the trailing `trailer` event.

amir: Could you paste the billing API call stack that records streams? I'm specifically looking for any code path that records both `on_chunk` and `on_trailer` without deduping by payload id.

jess: Snippet from the billing adapter (sanitized):
```
on_chunk(chunk) { tally += chunk.tokens; }
on_trailer(meta) { if (!meta._seen) { tally += meta.tokens; }
// but meta._seen is not set in reconnect path
}
```
jess: Looks like `_seen` is only set during the normal close flow, not during reconnection replay.

tom: OK — preliminary root cause: replayed trailer events during reconnects can bypass the dedupe flag and get double-counted. Fix path: either attach a stable stream-id+sequence to trailer events and use that for idempotency in billing, or ensure `on_trailer` uses the same dedupe marker even when the chunk came from a reconnection replay.

lina: Customer ask: can we issue a credit now and patch the billing records for INV-ACME-221? They need the corrected invoiced amount before EOD.

billing-bot: @tom — created ticket BILL-5823 for manual adjust; tentative credit amount = 71 tokens * token_unit_price => $0.0483 (estimated).

amir: I'll file a runtime PR to set `_seen=true` for replayed trailers and add idempotency keys on these meta events. Short-term we can run a ledger reconciliation script to subtract entries where request_id had >1 trailer record within 10s window.

jess: Repro guide for eng: use `curl -N` to stream, programmatically call `AbortController.abort()` after N ms, then reconnect with same `session` header to trigger replay. Example: 
```
# repro
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Session: acme-123" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate/stream?model=..."
# in client: abort and reconnect quickly with same X-Session
```
jess: I've created a small test harness in the infra sandbox (sandbox:stream-replay) to reproduce; assigned to @amir to push fix.

tom: For support response to ACME: propose immediate one-off credit and ETA for patch: credit processed today; patch and deploy in 24-48hrs; follow-up with reconciliation. Lina please confirm and ping when credit is issued.

lina: Sending that to the customer now. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

amir: I'll open the PR and link it here when ready. Expecting to have a hotfix branch by EOD.

billing-bot: BILL-5823 updated: status=pending-adjustment assigned=finance-team due=2387658000

lina: (closing notes) saved this thread to the incident board under billing/streaming-replay for postmortem follow-up.
